Messages.Author: jspektr
Messages.Body:
This is a rebuild of a deck I played and won with last night
(disclaimer: my first predator, a CEL/pot rush deck, got hand-jammed
right out the gate, and my prey, AUS/THAU intercept combat, rarely had
more than 2 intercept and not enough ways around S:CE from Majesty and
Toreador's Bane. In a more competitive environment, I probably would
have been obliterated).

Anyway, in the course of the game it occured to me that it's not that
hard to get the Daughters enough stealth for most situations, and
they're really, really good at voting (I had no problem getting up to
10 votes, with Charming Lobby(2), Bewitching Oration(3), Madrigal(2)
and Echo of Harmonies(2)). The main thing they're vulnerable to is
bleeds and rush. The solution seemed to be Domain Challenge (weenies
usually tap everything) and Banishment (get rid of big vamps).

Deck Name: Heathers

Crypt: (12 cards, Min: 12, Max: 23, Avg: 4.42)
----------------------------------------------
2 Muse ani for mel 3, Daughters of Cacophony
2 Celeste mel pre 3, Daughters of Cacophony
2 Delilah Monroe for MEL pre 4, Daughters of Cacophony
3 Angela Preston for MEL PRE 5, Daughters of Cacophony
3 Gael Pilet chi FOR MEL pre 6, Daughters of Cacophony

Library: (90 cards)
-------------------
Master (23 cards)
1 Barrens, The
1 Bastille Opera House
2 Creepshow Casino
2 Dreams of the Sphinx
1 Elder Library
2 Information Highway
2 Paris Opera House
2 Parthenon, The
5 Presence
1 Slave Auction
2 Tribute to the Master
2 Visit from the Capuchin

Action (14 cards)
2 Charming Lobby
12 Choir

Action Modifier (27 cards)
4 Bewitching Oration
3 Bribes
2 Business Pressure
4 Echo of Harmonies
2 Freak Drive
6 Missing Voice, The
2 Siren's Lure
4 Voter Captivation

Political Action (12 cards)
5 Banishment
2 Consanguineous Boon
3 Domain Challenge
2 Rumors of Gehenna

Combat (6 cards)
3 Majesty
3 Toreador's Bane

Combo (8 cards)
8 Madrigal

The strategy is to get Daughters out fast (with help from Dreams and
Info Highway), and tool them up with Presence to help the votes and
make Toreador's Bane more effective. The Parthenon and Rumors of
Gehenna will be crucial to making that work. Barrens, Capuchin and
Elder Library all help get the right combos into your hand.

Whenever possible, the Daughters vote. This requires a lot of watching
the table to see when you're least likely to be blocked or outvoted.
If serious intercept is out, you might have to wait for the Paris
Opera House or the Creepshow Casino to come out. When I played it, the
Missing Voice plus the inherent +1 stealth on votes was usually
enough. It's also important to not forget that any vote played can be
played a second time with Echo, which is especially good when the
first vote was Charming Lobbied (making Domain Challenge, in
particular, very nasty).

The Choirs mostly work to mess with the minds of potential blockers.
If they see the first inferior Choir come out, then blockers tend to
not block your second action if it's a vote, because they want to save
their intercept for the huge superior Choir at the end. Which may
never happen. It's usually worth wasting one Choir to get an important
vote through. If the Banishments do their job and leave your prey
open, that's about the only time the superior Choirs get used (though
at that point it might be better just to bleed with all the
Daughters).

Comments? The deck when played had less masters, more Choirs and
different votes (KRC and Autarkis Persecution, only 2 Banishments),
and required serious table playing to work right. Lots of bargaining
to get votes through and mind games to trick people into blocking the
wrong thing or assuming you had a S:CE in hand. Like I said earlier,
I'm not sure it would survive a more hard-core table, but it seems
like it has potential.

JSpektr

Messages.Author: Javelin
Messages.Body:
Some thoughts:

1. I believe you have too many Master cards, even for a 90-card deck.
With the speed at which you plan to cycle cards (considering 26 action
cards [including referendums] and 35 action modifiers [including
Madrigal]) you're almost assured of drawing more than two per turn.
This deck is reliant on drawing The Parthenon or Rumours of Gehenna
early - a bad thing, since if you DON'T draw one quickly, you won't be
able to easily cycle to one either (even with Visit or Dreams). With
that in mind, Slave Auction is a poor choice for the deck - you likely
won't have spare master phase actions to use it.

2. While I'm all for the idea of a "pure" DoC crypt, in practice,
permanent votes are always better than vote-gaining action modifiers.
No matter how many you have, you'll always face situations where all
you're drawing are political action cards, or just not enough
different types to get the vote through (say, you need both a
Bewitching Oration and a Madrigal but only have one). Negotiating with
other Methuselahs can offset this a bit, but it's hard to negotiate
with a Domain Challenge. Also, like Derek Ray has mentioned, you have
that "younger vampire" clause with the Banishment thing, so those
should probably be KRCs.
Anyway, for permanent votes, consider adding Toreador or Ventrue to
the crypt. Toreador because the Melpominee cards split with the Torrie
clan disciplines, Ventrue because they share two disciplines with the
DoC and let you include Ventrue Headquarters. The younger princes
(Tatiana Romanova, Timothy Crowley) would do nicely. Anson's ability
would be excellent with all the Master cards you want to use. Rake
would work with the deck, too. Another way to go about this is,
instead of using the higher capacity princes, put in younger vampires
(Gideon, Violette) and some Praxis Seizures, which Angela Preston can
use. Incidentally, this is why I suggested the Camarilla clans instead
of the antitribu - better to let Angela (with MEL and PRE) use a
Praxis Seizure, than to have Muse (with just mel) try to pass a
Crusade.

3. Vulnerability to bleeds is the main problem with DoC. Since this is
a vote deck, you can include some Protected Resources, then never
bleed so it stays in play indefinitely. Or, if you do add Toreador or
Ventrue, you can add a bit of bounce. Rush shouldn't be a problem, not
when Daughters have Fortitude. Use a few copies of Skin of Steel and
Superior Mettle to go with the Majesty and Toreador's Bane - if they
Immortal Grapple, prevent damage; if they don't, end combat. It works
for the Ventrue, it should work for the DoC.

4. Your choices of vote-gaining modifiers could use some improvements.
My thoughts:
a) if your deck includes Bewitching Oration, Madrigal and Charming
Lobby, you don't need Bribes
b) ditto with Business Pressure - if you're willing to spend
blood/pool to gain votes, use Awe
c) good idea to use Awe anyway, because Awe + Voter Captivation =
great combo (with PRE)

5. I would just get rid of Choir completely. The bluff factor doesn't
give enough of a benefit to justify including them, and 12 copies
isn't enough to make it a viable secondary offensive strategy. Better
to focus on the politics.

The Banishment change was long overdue; original card text harshly
penalized playing with larger vampires, because the mechanics of the
game dictate that large vampires are NEVER worth as much pool as you
spend them. This leads to most large vampires spending significant
portions of each game on half or less blood, making them excellent
Banishment targets.

automatically pitch up to 2 pool against it while it's passing, since
he'll be losing 3 anyway. Sometimes, this works in your favor when you
have a surprise Awe; sometimes you just have to take the free bleed for
2.

I'm not saying I don't understand the reasoning behind it. I think
it's a good change. Whether or not the change is good has nothing to
do with my complaint that you have to double-check every single card
you put in your deck against the latest list of changes, just in case.
Almost every time we play, someone has to pull out the list of changes
to check something, and often someone's deck concept will be shot
because they didn't realize an important card was changed. We're good
natured about it, but it's still irritating.

It would be nice if there was an economical way for White Wolf to
reprint all the cards with significant text changes, and then just
sell them as singles. I'd happily buy new Banishments, Elysiums, and
other changed cards just so I had the real card text in front of me on
the actual card I'm playing. Sure, this can be done to a limited
extent now, but I bought several boxes of Final Nights and didn't get
enough changed cards to replace all the old ones I have. Some cards
that got changed only appeared in places like the Sabbat Wars

I usually put the Business Pressure out first if it's available, and
then keep other vote mods in reserve. People frequently forget Echo of
Harmonies is played by non-acting minions, making it easy to get in
two, four, or even six surprise votes. Again, it's up to playing the
table, if you pull out a Business Pressure on an important vote that
changes the balance of the table, a lot of pool can end up getting
spent, weakening everyone.

I'm looking at changing the deck around a bit, and throwing in a
couple of Red Herrings and Mirror Images, along with 3 Chimestry
master cards and 8 Sanguine Instructions (taking out the Choirs and
some master cards). The idea is to use Gael's inherent inferior
Chimestry with a skill card and Sanguine Instruction to boost
everyone's capacity and make the Banishments more usable (one of the
other Daughters can SI Gael for superior Presence). Gael can also SI
with Fortitude.

Fame (controller of famous vamp loses pool)
Immortal Grapple (no longer lasts entire combat)

and I'm not sure ANYONE doesn't know the IG ruling these days, what with
how much in demand they were. All the rest of the cards are of
ridiculous simplicity: Resilience, "prevent 3 non-agg damage".

which changed the card's basic function; Taste still reads "I gain
blood", Signpost still reads "I hit harder". Finding out the Immortal
Grapple ruling as a surprise wouldn't break a deck, as it still performs
mostly the same as before.
